source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 19 (PDF 38-58, printed 35-55); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 19 (Basics of Organic Chemistry), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The number of carbon containing compounds known today is more than:
blocks.explanation: We are familiar with more than 20 million carbon containing compounds, most of them studied in organic chemistry (19.1).

book_ref.quote: Today, we are familiar with more than 20 million carbon containing compounds

blocks.prompt: 2 According to IUPAC, organic chemistry is the study of compounds containing carbon bonded to itself, hydrogen or other elements:
blocks.explanation: IUPAC defines organic chemistry as the study of carbon compounds excluding some inorganic compounds such as carbonates, cyanides, CO₂ and CO (19.1).

book_ref.quote: the study of compounds containing carbon, where carbon is bonded to itself, hydrogen, or other elements

blocks.prompt: 3 Which one of the following is excluded from organic chemistry although it contains carbon?
blocks.explanation: Carbonates, cyanides (e.g. KCN), CO₂ and CO are traditional inorganic compounds excluded from organic chemistry (19.1; the printed 'KCl' is corrected to KCN).

book_ref.quote: which are excluded from organic chemistry are carbonates

blocks.prompt: 4 Organic compounds are generally distinguished from inorganic compounds by their:

options.text: high melting points and high solubility in water
high densities and high boiling points
low melting points, low densities and low solubility in water
ionic nature and high melting points

blocks.explanation: Organic compounds have low m.p's, b.p's, low densities and low solubility in water (19.1).

book_ref.quote: Organic compounds can be easily distinguished from inorganic compounds by their unique properties

blocks.prompt: 5 The ability of self-linkage between atoms of the same element is called:
blocks.explanation: Catenation (Latin catena = chain) is the self-linkage of atoms of the same element (19.1).

book_ref.quote: The ability of self-linkage between the atoms of the same element is known as catenation

blocks.prompt: 6 Carbon forms long chains and rings through:
blocks.explanation: Carbon forms long chains and rings through stable C–C covalent bonds; this self-linking property is catenation (19.1).

book_ref.quote: Carbon forms long chains and rings through the stable

blocks.prompt: 7 According to the chapter, the number of different arrangements possible with four carbon atoms is:
blocks.explanation: The tetravalent nature of carbon gives many arrangements; with four carbon atoms there are four different arrangements (19.1).

book_ref.quote: with four carbon atoms, there are four different arrangements

blocks.prompt: 8 The large variety of arrangements of carbon atoms in compounds is mainly due to carbon being:
blocks.explanation: The tetravalent nature of carbon enables it to have many different arrangements, giving a variety of compounds (19.1).

book_ref.quote: Tetravalent nature of carbon enables it to have much more different ways of arrangements

blocks.prompt: 9 Why are organic compounds complex, with large structures and vast diversity?

options.text: because of their high melting points

blocks.explanation: Catenation explains why organic compounds are complex, having large structures and vast diversity (19.1).

book_ref.quote: Catenation explains why organic compounds are complex, having large structures and vast diversity

blocks.text: 19.2 Hydrocarbons (Compounds of Carbon and Hydrogen Only)

blocks.prompt: 10 Compounds containing carbon and hydrogen only are called:
blocks.explanation: Hydrocarbons are compounds containing carbon and hydrogen only (19.2).

book_ref.quote: Compounds containing carbon and hydrogen only in their molecules are called hydrocarbons

blocks.prompt: 11 Hydrocarbons are broadly classified into two types on the basis of their:
blocks.explanation: On the basis of carbon skeleton, hydrocarbons are open chain (aliphatic) or closed chain (cyclic) (19.2).

book_ref.quote: On the basis of carbon skeleton, hydrocarbons are broadly classified into two types

blocks.prompt: 12 The word 'aliphatic' comes from the Greek word aleiphatos, which means:
blocks.explanation: Aleiphatos means fat; fats have open chain structure, so open chain hydrocarbons are called aliphatic (19.2).

book_ref.quote: aleiphatos is a Greek word meaning fat

blocks.prompt: 13 Alkenes and alkynes are classified as:
blocks.explanation: Aliphatic hydrocarbons are subdivided into saturated (alkanes) and unsaturated (alkenes and alkynes) (19.2).

book_ref.quote: These can be further subdivided into saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes)

blocks.prompt: 14 Hydrocarbons possessing rings of carbon atoms are called:
blocks.explanation: Hydrocarbons with rings of carbon atoms are closed chain or cyclic hydrocarbons (19.2).

book_ref.quote: Hydrocarbons possessing rings of carbon atoms are called closed chain or cyclic hydrocarbons

blocks.prompt: 15 Cycloalkanes and cycloalkenes, which are cyclic but behave like aliphatic hydrocarbons, are called:
blocks.explanation: Cyclic hydrocarbons, saturated or unsaturated, which behave like aliphatic hydrocarbons are alicyclic, e.g. cycloalkanes, cycloalkenes (19.2).

book_ref.quote: which behave like aliphatic hydrocarbons, are called alicyclic hydrocarbons

blocks.prompt: 16 Which one of the following is an aromatic hydrocarbon?
blocks.explanation: Cyclic hydrocarbons having a benzene ring or resembling structures are aromatic, e.g. benzene, naphthalene, diphenyl methane (19.2).

book_ref.quote: having benzene ring or resembling structures are called aromatic hydrocarbons

blocks.prompt: 17 Open chain hydrocarbons are also called:
blocks.explanation: Hydrocarbons with an open chain of carbon atoms are open chain or acyclic, more commonly aliphatic, hydrocarbons (19.2).

book_ref.quote: Hydrocarbons possessing open chain of carbon atoms are called open chain or acyclic hydrocarbons

blocks.prompt: 18 An atom or group of atoms, or a double or triple bond, which determines the characteristic properties of an organic compound is called:
blocks.explanation: This is the definition of a functional group (19.3).

book_ref.quote: which determines the characteristic properties of an organic compound is called functional group

blocks.prompt: 19 Methanol and ethanol are liquids while methane and ethane are gases at room temperature because alcohols:

options.text: form hydrogen bonds through their –OH group

blocks.explanation: The hydroxyl group (–OH) of alcohols can form hydrogen bonds; alkanes have no such functional group (19.3).

book_ref.quote: Methanol and ethanol are liquids while methane and ethane are gases

blocks.prompt: 20 The melting and boiling points of alcohols are higher than those of their corresponding:
blocks.explanation: m.p and b.p of alcohols are higher than those of the corresponding alkanes (methanol vs methane, ethanol vs ethane) because of hydrogen bonding (19.3, book correction: alkanes, not alkenes).

book_ref.quote: The comparison is with the corresponding alkanes (methanol with methane, ethanol with ethane)

blocks.prompt: 21 Glucose and sucrose are soluble in water because they:
blocks.explanation: Lower alcohols, carboxylic acids, glucose and sucrose dissolve in polar solvents like water due to their polar functional groups (19.3).

book_ref.quote: are soluble in polar solvents like water due to their polar functional groups

blocks.prompt: 22 The types of organic compounds are dictated by the polarity of the bond and the ______ in their functional groups.
blocks.explanation: The two factors are polarity of the bond and bond order, i.e. the number of bonds in the functional group (19.3).

book_ref.quote: Bond order i.e. number of bonds in the functional group

blocks.prompt: 23 Which pair has no functional group?
blocks.explanation: Alkanes and cycloalkanes have no functional group: no charges, no polarity and no double or triple bonds (19.3).

book_ref.quote: Alkanes and cycloalkanes have no functional group in them

blocks.prompt: 24 The nature of the functional group of an organic compound affects:

options.text: both its physical and chemical properties

blocks.explanation: Both physical and chemical properties are highly affected by the nature of the functional groups (19.3).

book_ref.quote: Both physical and chemical properties of organic compounds are highly affected by the nature of functional groups

blocks.prompt: 25 The rules for the systematic nomenclature of organic compounds were formulated by:
blocks.explanation: IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) formulated rules for systematic nomenclature (19.4).

book_ref.quote: A set of rules was thus formulated by IUPAC

blocks.prompt: 26 The systematic (IUPAC) name of an organic compound is based on the:
blocks.explanation: The IUPAC name is based on the parent hydrocarbon and consists of root, suffix and prefix (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The systematic or IUPAC name of an organic compound is based on the parent hydrocarbon

blocks.prompt: 27 The stem or root of an IUPAC name gives:

options.text: the longest continuous carbon chain including the carbon bearing the functional group
the name of the side chain
the family name of the compound

blocks.explanation: The stem gives the longest continuous carbon chain including the functional-group carbon (19.4 i).

book_ref.quote: It gives the longest continuous carbon chain including the carbon bearing the functional group

blocks.prompt: 28 While numbering the parent chain, the lowest possible number is given to the carbon bearing:
blocks.explanation: Lowest possible number is given to the carbon bearing the functional group (19.4 i).

book_ref.quote: Lowest possible number is given to the carbon bearing the functional group

blocks.prompt: 29 If the carbon atoms of the parent chain are joined in a ring, the name starts with:
blocks.explanation: For carbon atoms joined in a ring, the name is started by 'cyclo' (19.4 i).

book_ref.quote: If the carbon atoms are joined in a ring, the name is started by

blocks.prompt: 30 The primary suffix in an IUPAC name indicates:

options.text: the family name of the compound
the name of the side chain
whether the parent chain is saturated or unsaturated

blocks.explanation: The primary suffix (suffix of stem or root) shows whether the parent chain is saturated or unsaturated (19.4 ii).

book_ref.quote: It indicates whether the parent chain is saturated or unsaturated

blocks.prompt: 31 The secondary suffix (suffix of the key functional group) gives:

options.text: the length of the parent chain
the family name of the compound

blocks.explanation: The secondary suffix gives the family name of the compound (19.4 ii).

book_ref.quote: Secondary suffix, also called suffix of the key functional group

blocks.prompt: 32 In an IUPAC name, the prefix gives:

options.text: the side chain or substituent with the number of the carbon to which it is attached

blocks.explanation: The prefix names the side chain (alkyl group) or substituent (halo, nitro, etc.) with the number of its carbon (19.4 iii).

book_ref.quote: It gives the name of the side chain (alkyl group) or any substituent

blocks.prompt: 33 If there is no prefix, the systematic name consists of:
blocks.explanation: If prefix is absent, the systematic name consists of root and suffix (19.4 iii).

book_ref.quote: If prefix is absent, then systematic name will consist of root and suffix

blocks.prompt: 34 In the name 3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol, the part 'en' is the:

options.text: primary suffix showing a double bond

blocks.explanation: 'but' is the stem (four carbons), 'en' the primary suffix (unsaturated, C=C), 'ol' the secondary suffix (alcohol family) and '3-methyl' the prefix (19.4).

book_ref.quote: 4-chlorobutanal and 3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol

blocks.prompt: 35 The stem used in the IUPAC name of a compound whose parent chain has four carbon atoms is:
blocks.explanation: The stem for four carbons is 'but', e.g. 4-chlorobutanal (19.4; book correction: not 'prop').

book_ref.quote: the stem for four carbons is

blocks.prompt: 36 The IUPAC class name of alkyl halides is:
blocks.explanation: Alkyl halides (CₙH₂ₙ₊₁X) are named halogenoalkanes, more precisely monohaloalkanes (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is halogenoalkane (more precisely monohaloalkane)

blocks.prompt: 37 The correct IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₂–I is:
blocks.explanation: Prefixes are written in alphabetical order (iodo before methyl), so the name is 1-iodo-3-methylbutane (19.4, book correction).

book_ref.quote: The substituent prefixes are written in alphabetical order

blocks.prompt: 38 Using the general formula of alkyl halides, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁X, the molecular formula of the alkyl chloride with n = 3 is:
blocks.explanation: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁X with n = 3: 2(3) + 1 = 7, so C₃H₇Cl (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is halogenoalkane (more precisely monohaloalkane)

blocks.prompt: 39 The IUPAC name of the class of alcohols ends in:
blocks.explanation: Alcohols are alkanols, e.g. methanol, propan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanol.

blocks.prompt: 40 From the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂O, the molecular formula of an alcohol with four carbon atoms is:
blocks.explanation: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂O with n = 4: 2(4) + 2 = 10, so C₄H₁₀O (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanol.

blocks.prompt: 41 The IUPAC name of H–C(=O)–H is:
blocks.explanation: Aldehydes are alkanals; HCHO is methanal (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanal.

blocks.prompt: 42 The correct condensed formula of 3-methylbutanal is:
blocks.explanation: Carbon 4 of 3-methylbutanal is CH₃, not CH₄: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–C(=O)–H (19.4, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Carbon 4 of 3-methylbutanal is a methyl group

blocks.prompt: 43 The IUPAC name of CH₃–C(=O)–CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: Ketones are alkanones; CH₃COCH₃ is propanone (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanone

blocks.prompt: 44 Aldehydes and ketones have the same general formula. A ketone and an aldehyde each with three carbon atoms both have the molecular formula:
blocks.explanation: Both follow CₙH₂ₙO; for n = 3, C₃H₆O (propanone and propanal) (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanone

blocks.prompt: 45 The IUPAC name of CH₃–COOH is:
blocks.explanation: Carboxylic acids are alkanoic acids; CH₃COOH is ethanoic acid (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanoic acid

blocks.prompt: 46 The IUPAC name of CH₃–C(=O)–NH₂ is:
blocks.explanation: Acid amides are alkanamides; CH₃CONH₂ is ethanamide (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanamide

blocks.prompt: 47 The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)–Cl is:
blocks.explanation: Acid halides are alkanoyl halides; CH₃CH₂COCl has three carbons: propanoyl chloride (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanoyl halides

blocks.prompt: 48 The IUPAC name of CH₃–C(=O)–O–CH₂–CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: Esters are alkyl alkanoates; the alkyl on oxygen is ethyl and the acid part has two carbons (ethanoate) (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkyl alkanoate

blocks.prompt: 49 The functional group –C(=O)–O–C(=O)– is present in:
blocks.explanation: –C(=O)–O–C(=O)– is the acid anhydride group, named alkanoic anhydride, e.g. ethanoic anhydride (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanoic anhydride

blocks.prompt: 50 Ethers are named in the IUPAC system as:
blocks.explanation: Ethers (–C–O–C–) are alkoxyalkanes, e.g. methoxymethane, ethoxyethane (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkoxyalkane.

blocks.prompt: 51 The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH₂–O–CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: The smaller group is named as alkoxy and the larger as the alkane: methoxyethane (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkoxyalkane.

blocks.prompt: 52 The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(NH₂)–CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: It is a primary amine (alkanamine) with NH₂ on carbon 2 of a three-carbon chain: propan-2-amine (19.4).

book_ref.quote: There are three types of amines

blocks.prompt: 53 In a secondary amine such as N-methylpropan-1-amine, the nitrogen atom carries:
blocks.explanation: In a secondary amine the nitrogen carries one hydrogen: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–NH–CH₃ (19.4, book correction; with NH₂ nitrogen would have four bonds).

book_ref.quote: In a secondary amine the nitrogen carries one hydrogen

blocks.prompt: 54 CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–N(CH₃)–CH₃ is a tertiary amine named:
blocks.explanation: Two identical methyl groups on N give the N,N-dialkylalkanamine name N,N-dimethylpropan-1-amine (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The class names are N,N-dialkylalkanamine and N-alkyl-N-alkylalkanamine

blocks.prompt: 55 The IUPAC name of CH₃–CN is:
blocks.explanation: Alkyl cyanides are alkanenitriles; the CN carbon is counted, so CH₃CN (two carbons) is ethanenitrile (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is alkanenitrile

blocks.prompt: 56 The correct IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CN is:
blocks.explanation: The name is 2-methylpropanenitrile (19.4, book correction of the misprint 'propaneritrile').

book_ref.quote: The name is 2-methylpropanenitrile.

blocks.prompt: 57 The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(NO₂)–CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: Nitroalkanes are named nitroalkane; NO₂ on carbon 2 of propane gives 2-nitropropane (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is nitroalkane

blocks.prompt: 58 Using the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁NO₂, the molecular formula of the nitroalkane with n = 2 is:
blocks.explanation: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁NO₂ with n = 2: 2(2) + 1 = 5, so C₂H₅NO₂ (nitroethane) (19.4).

book_ref.quote: The IUPAC name is nitroalkane

blocks.prompt: 59 Which one of the following is NOT a type of structural formula described in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: Structural formulae are displayed, condensed and skeletal; the empirical formula only gives the simplest ratio (19.5).

book_ref.quote: There are different types of formulae which are used to represent organic compounds

blocks.prompt: 60 The formula which represents the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule is the:
blocks.explanation: The molecular formula gives the actual number of atoms of each element, e.g. butane C₄H₁₀ (19.5).

book_ref.quote: represents the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule

blocks.prompt: 61 Ethanol and methoxymethane both have the molecular formula:
blocks.explanation: Ethanol and methoxymethane are different compounds with the same molecular formula C₂H₆O (19.5).

book_ref.quote: ethanol and methoxymethane are represented by same molecular formula

blocks.prompt: 62 Two different compounds can have the same molecular formula because a molecular formula gives no information about:

options.text: the sequence of linking of atoms and the functional group

blocks.explanation: A molecular formula tells nothing about the sequence of linking of atoms or the nature of the functional group (19.5).

book_ref.quote: molecular formula gives no information about the sequence in which atoms are linked together

blocks.prompt: 63 The empirical formula of hexane, C₆H₁₄, is:
blocks.explanation: The empirical formula is the smallest whole number ratio: C₆H₁₄ ÷ 2 = C₃H₇ (19.5).

book_ref.quote: represents the smallest whole number ratio of atoms of each element

blocks.prompt: 64 Glucose has the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. Its empirical formula is:
blocks.explanation: Divide by the common factor 6: C₆H₁₂O₆ → CH₂O, the same empirical formula as ethanoic acid (19.5).

book_ref.quote: empirical formula of butane (C₄H₁₀) is C₂H₅

blocks.prompt: 65 For which compound are the empirical and molecular formulae the same?
blocks.explanation: C₃H₆O₂ (3 : 6 : 2) has no common factor, so empirical = molecular; C₄H₁₀ → C₂H₅, C₂H₄O₂ → CH₂O, C₄H₈O₂ → C₂H₄O (19.5).

book_ref.quote: The formula which represents the smallest whole number ratio of atoms

blocks.prompt: 66 Which formula shows the number of each kind of atom and also the sequence in which they are joined?
blocks.explanation: The structural formula shows both the number of each kind of atom and the sequence of joining (19.5).

book_ref.quote: not only shows the number of each kind of atom in the molecule but also the sequence

blocks.prompt: 67 The formula which shows all the bonds between atoms, including the type of bonds and positions of functional groups, is the:
blocks.explanation: The displayed (graphical) formula is the most complete, self-explanatory form of the structural formula (19.5).

book_ref.quote: which shows all the bonds between different atoms including the type of bonds

blocks.prompt: 68 The condensed formula of butane is:
blocks.explanation: In a condensed (linear) formula single bonds are omitted and middle methylene groups are bracketed: CH₃(CH₂)₂CH₃ (19.5).

book_ref.quote: single covalent bonds are omitted, however, branches, functional groups

blocks.prompt: 69 A displayed formula is often condensed into a one-line structure because it:
blocks.explanation: Displayed formula uses a lot of space, so it is condensed into a one-line (condensed or linear) formula (19.5).

book_ref.quote: Displayed formula uses a lot of space

blocks.prompt: 70 In a skeletal (bond-line) formula:

options.text: symbols of C and H and the C–H bonds are removed

blocks.explanation: Skeletal formula removes C and H symbols and C–H bonds; C–C bonds are lines meeting at angles, and multiple bonds and functional groups are shown (19.5).

book_ref.quote: all the symbols of carbon and hydrogen atoms as well as the carbon to hydrogen bonds are removed

blocks.prompt: 71 In a skeletal formula, the number of hydrogen atoms on each carbon is understood from the fact that each carbon:

options.text: makes a total of three bonds
makes a total of four bonds

blocks.explanation: Each carbon is assumed to form enough C–H bonds to make a total of four bonds (19.5).

book_ref.quote: Each carbon is assumed to form enough

blocks.prompt: 72 In a skeletal formula, each joint of two lines represents:
blocks.explanation: Each line is a bond and each joint shows a carbon atom; double lines are double bonds (19.6).

book_ref.quote: Each line represents a bond and each joint shows a carbon atom

blocks.prompt: 73 A skeletal formula is a zig-zag of four single lines with no atom symbols shown. Its molecular formula is:
blocks.explanation: Four lines have 5 points (2 ends + 3 joints) = 5 C; completing four bonds on each C gives 12 H: C₅H₁₂ (19.6).

book_ref.quote: Count one C atom at the end of each line unless another atom is shown there

blocks.prompt: 74 A skeletal formula is a zig-zag of three single lines with OH written at one end. Its molecular formula is:
blocks.explanation: Three lines join four points; the one carrying OH is the O atom, so 3 C. H = 7 on carbons + 1 on O = 8: C₃H₈O (propan-1-ol) (19.6).

book_ref.quote: Count the C atoms represented and the heteroatoms shown in the skeleton

blocks.prompt: 75 A skeletal formula is a regular pentagon drawn with single lines only. Its empirical formula is:
blocks.explanation: Five joints = 5 C; each ring carbon needs 2 H: C₅H₁₀ (cyclopentane); dividing by 5 gives the empirical formula CH₂ (19.6).

book_ref.quote: Count the number of H atoms necessary to complete the octet of each C atom

blocks.prompt: 76 The empirical formula of ethanamide, CH₃CONH₂, is:
blocks.explanation: CH₃CONH₂ is its structural formula; C₂H₅NO (2 : 5 : 1 : 1) cannot be simplified, so empirical = molecular (19.6, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Its empirical formula is C₂H₅NO, the same as its molecular formula

blocks.prompt: 77 In a skeletal formula, a double line between two joints represents:
blocks.explanation: Double lines represent double bonds (19.6).

book_ref.quote: Each line represents a bond and each joint shows a carbon atom

blocks.prompt: 78 Homolytic fission of a covalent bond occurs when the bond is:
blocks.explanation: Homolytic fission occurs in a nonpolar bond; the shared pair is shared equally between the two atoms (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: Homolytic fission occurs when the breaking bond is nonpolar

blocks.prompt: 79 Homolysis of a Cl–Cl bond gives:
blocks.explanation: In homolysis each atom takes one electron of the shared pair, giving two Cl• free radicals (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: the two shared electrons in the bond are distributed equally between the two atoms

blocks.prompt: 80 Atoms or groups of atoms with unpaired electrons are called:
blocks.explanation: Atoms or groups with unpaired electrons, formed in homolysis, are free radicals (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: These atoms or groups of atoms with unpaired electrons are called free radicals

blocks.prompt: 81 Free radicals are highly reactive because:

options.text: their unpaired electrons tend to be paired

blocks.explanation: Free radicals are reactive intermediates because their unpaired electrons tend to be paired (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: are highly reactive because of the tendency of their unpaired electrons to be paired

blocks.prompt: 82 In heterolytic fission, the atom that keeps both shared electrons:
blocks.explanation: In heterolysis one atom keeps both electrons (negative charge); the other, short of one electron, becomes positive (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: One of the atoms keeps both electrons, and it acquires a negative charge

blocks.prompt: 83 Heterolytic fission occurs when the breaking bond is:
blocks.explanation: Heterolytic fission occurs when the breaking bond is polar; the shared electrons go unequally (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: Heterolytic fission occurs when the breaking bond is polar

blocks.prompt: 84 A species containing a carbon atom with a positive charge is called a:
blocks.explanation: A species with a positively charged carbon is a carbocation (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: A species which contains a carbon atom with a positive charge is known as carbocation

blocks.prompt: 85 A carbanion is formed when carbon is bonded to an atom which is:

options.text: more electronegative than carbon, e.g. O
less electronegative than carbon, e.g. Li or Mg

blocks.explanation: Carbanion forms when carbon is bonded to a metal less electronegative than carbon, e.g. Li, Mg, Cd (19.7 A).

book_ref.quote: Carbanion is formed when carbon is bonded to a heteroatom (metal)

blocks.prompt: 86 Heterolysis of the C–Cl bond in (CH₃)₃C–Cl gives:
blocks.explanation: Cl is more electronegative than carbon and keeps the shared pair, so a carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺ and Cl⁻ form (19.7 A). (P is not such an atom: 2.2 < 2.5.)

book_ref.quote: Phosphorus (electronegativity 2.2) is less electronegative than carbon (2.5)

blocks.prompt: 87 In a reaction, the species which is attacked is called the:
blocks.explanation: The attacking species is the reagent; the species undergoing attack is the substrate (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: the attacking species is called reagent and the species which is undergoing attack is called the substrate

blocks.prompt: 88 Which one of the following is a free radical?
blocks.explanation: Free radicals have unpaired electrons, e.g. Cl•, H•, •CH₃, CH₃COO• (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: An atom or group of atoms having unpaired electrons are called free radicals e.g

blocks.prompt: 89 An electrophile is a species which:

options.text: donates a pair of electrons to form a new bond
accepts a pair of electrons to form a new bond

blocks.explanation: An electrophile (electron lover) accepts an electron pair to form a new bond (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: able to accept a pair of electrons to form a new bond is called an electrophile

blocks.prompt: 90 Which one of the following is a neutral electrophile?
blocks.explanation: Electrophiles are positive ions or neutral molecules such as SO₃ and BF₃; NH₃ and H₂O are nucleophiles (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: Electrophiles (electron lovers) are either positive ions (including carbocations) or neutral molecules

blocks.prompt: 91 Which one of the following is an electrophile?
blocks.explanation: NO₂⁺ is a positive ion and accepts an electron pair; CN⁻, ROH and Br⁻ are nucleophiles (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: e.g. CH₃⁺, H⁺, Br⁺, NO₂⁺, SO₃, BF₃

blocks.prompt: 92 A nucleophile is a species which is able to:

options.text: donate a pair of electrons to form a new bond
accept a proton only from carbon

blocks.explanation: A nucleophile (nucleus lover) donates an electron pair to form a new bond (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: able to donate a pair of electrons to form a new bond is called nucleophile

blocks.prompt: 93 Which one of the following is a neutral nucleophile?
blocks.explanation: Nucleophiles are negative ions or neutral molecules with electron pairs, e.g. NH₃, H₂O, ROH (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: Nucleophiles (nucleus lovers) are either negative ions

blocks.prompt: 94 In CH₃–Li, the carbon atom is:
blocks.explanation: Li is less electronegative, so carbon carries δ– and is nucleophilic while Li is δ+ and electrophilic; in CH₃–OH it is the reverse (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: they carry partial charges, which can also make them electrophilic or nucleophilic

blocks.prompt: 95 In methanol, CH₃–OH, the carbon of CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: Polar molecules carry partial charges: in CH₃–OH carbon is δ+ (electrophilic) and OH is δ– (nucleophilic) (19.7 B).

book_ref.quote: The terms electrophilic and nucleophilic do not apply only to ions

blocks.prompt: 96 How many types of organic reactions are described in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: Seven types are described: substitution, addition, elimination, hydrolysis, condensation, oxidation, reduction (19.7 C; book correction: not four).

book_ref.quote: Seven types are described below (i–vii), not four.

blocks.prompt: 97 CH₃–CH₂–Br + KOH(aq) → CH₃–CH₂–OH + KBr is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Br is replaced by OH and two products form: a substitution reaction (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: an atom or group of atoms in one molecule is replaced by another atom or group of atoms

blocks.prompt: 98 In an addition reaction, two reactants react to produce:
blocks.explanation: In addition reactions two reactants give a single product, e.g. ethene + H₂ → ethane (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: In addition reactions, two reactants react to produce a single product

blocks.prompt: 99 Ethene adds hydrogen in the presence of nickel to give ethane at a temperature of:
blocks.explanation: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃–CH₃ over Ni at 200–300 °C (19.7 C, book correction of the printed unit).

book_ref.quote: The temperature for this hydrogenation is 200–300 °C.

blocks.prompt: 100 The main product of the addition of HBr to propene, CH₃–CH=CH₂, is:
blocks.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule the main product is 2-bromopropane, CH₃–CHBr–CH₃ (19.7 C, book correction).

book_ref.quote: the main product with HBr is 2-bromopropane

blocks.prompt: 101 Bromoethane heated with alcoholic KOH gives:
blocks.explanation: With alcoholic KOH, H and Br are removed from adjacent carbons forming CH₂=CH₂, ethene (elimination) (19.7 C; book correction: ethene, not ethane).

book_ref.quote: removal of atoms or groups of atoms from two adjacent atoms in the substrate molecule

blocks.prompt: 102 Elimination reactions are regarded as the reverse of:
blocks.explanation: Elimination forms a multiple bond; addition removes it, so elimination is regarded as the reverse of addition (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: Elimination reactions are regarded as reverse of addition reactions

blocks.prompt: 103 Ethyl ethanoate reacts with water in the presence of H⁺ to give:
blocks.explanation: Hydrolysis: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH, catalysed by H⁺ (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: a compound breaks into two on reaction with water often helped by

blocks.prompt: 104 Propanone reacts with hydroxylamine to form propanone oxime and water. This is a:
blocks.explanation: Two molecules combine into a bigger molecule with loss of H₂O: condensation (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: two molecules combine to form a bigger molecule with or without loss of a smaller molecule

blocks.prompt: 105 An organic molecule is said to be oxidized when it:
blocks.explanation: Oxidation: loss of electrons, gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, more C–O bonds or higher oxidation state of carbon (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: increase in number of bonds of carbon with oxygen or increase in oxidation state of carbon

blocks.prompt: 106 Propene treated with O₃ followed by Zn/H₂O gives:
blocks.explanation: CH₃–CH=CH₂ with O₃, Zn/H₂O gives CH₃CHO (ethanal) + HCHO (methanal): an oxidation (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: Loss of electron is called oxidation

blocks.prompt: 107 Which change in carbon shows reduction?

options.text: increase in the oxidation state of carbon
decrease in the number of bonds of carbon with oxygen

blocks.explanation: Reduction: gain of electrons or hydrogen, loss of oxygen, fewer C–O bonds or lower oxidation state of carbon (19.7 C).

book_ref.quote: Reduction is a reaction where gain of electron, loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen

blocks.prompt: 108 There are basically how many types of reagents?

options.text: three: free radicals, electrophiles and nucleophiles
four: free radicals, ions, acids and bases

blocks.explanation: The basic statements: two ways of bond breaking and three types of reagents, free radicals, electrophiles and nucleophiles (19.7).

book_ref.quote: There are basically three types of reagents

blocks.prompt: 109 The pathway of a reaction showing the breaking and making of bonds in the substrate is called its:
blocks.explanation: A mechanism is the pathway showing breaking and making of bonds leading to the product (19.8).

book_ref.quote: A mechanism is the pathway adapted by a reaction showing the breaking and making of bonds

blocks.prompt: 110 Reaction mechanisms are divided into free radical and ionic (polar) types depending upon the nature of:
blocks.explanation: Depending upon the nature of reagents, mechanisms are free radical or ionic (polar) (19.8).

book_ref.quote: Depending upon the nature of reagents, reaction mechanisms are divided into two main types

blocks.prompt: 111 A free radical mechanism involves:
blocks.explanation: The free radical mechanism involves homolysis, producing free radicals that attack the substrate (19.8).

book_ref.quote: It involves homolysis during which free radicals are produced

blocks.prompt: 112 The correct sequence of steps in a free radical reaction is:
blocks.explanation: Initial radicals form in initiation, generate more radicals in propagation, and combine in termination (19.8).

book_ref.quote: The reaction involves initiation where initial free radicals are produced

blocks.prompt: 113 A free radical reaction comes to an end in the termination step by:

options.text: combination of free radicals of the same or different types

blocks.explanation: Termination: free radicals of the same or different types combine (19.8).

book_ref.quote: Finally, the reaction terminates by combining the free radicals of the same or different types

blocks.prompt: 114 Methane reacts with excess chlorine in diffused sunlight. The final product formed when all four hydrogens are replaced is:
blocks.explanation: CH₄ + 4Cl₂ → CCl₄ + 4HCl in diffused sunlight, by a free radical mechanism (19.8).

book_ref.quote: These radicals generate more radicals in the propagation step

blocks.prompt: 115 An ionic or polar mechanism involves:
blocks.explanation: The polar mechanism involves heterolysis, producing electrophiles and nucleophiles that attack polar substrates (19.8).

book_ref.quote: It involves heterolysis, during which electrophiles and nucleophiles are produced

blocks.prompt: 116 In OH⁻ + CH₃Br → CH₃OH + Br⁻, the bromide ion is called the:
blocks.explanation: In nucleophilic substitution OH⁻ attacks the saturated electrophilic carbon and replaces Br⁻, the leaving group (19.8).

book_ref.quote: a nucleophile attacks on a saturated electrophilic carbon and substitutes another nucleophile called leaving group

blocks.prompt: 117 Hydroxide ion reacts with bromomethane to give methanol. The mechanism is:
blocks.explanation: OH⁻ (nucleophile) replaces Br on a saturated carbon through a transition state: nucleophilic substitution (19.8).

book_ref.quote: hydroxide ion and bromomethane give methanol through a transition state

blocks.prompt: 118 In nucleophilic addition, the nucleophile attacks:

options.text: the electrophilic carbon of a carbonyl compound
a saturated carbon bearing a halogen

blocks.explanation: In nucleophilic addition, a nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon to give an addition product (19.8).

book_ref.quote: a nucleophile attacks on electrophilic carbon of a carbonyl compound to give addition product

blocks.prompt: 119 The product of nucleophilic addition of cyanide ion (HCN) to ethanal is:
blocks.explanation: CN⁻ adds to the carbonyl carbon of ethanal, giving 2-hydroxypropanenitrile (19.8).

book_ref.quote: cyanide ion adds to ethanal, giving 2-hydroxypropanenitrile

blocks.prompt: 120 Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give bromoethane. The reaction is:
blocks.explanation: The electrophile attacks the electron-rich C=C, giving bromoethane: electrophilic addition (19.8).

book_ref.quote: an electrophile attacks on an electron rich position (nucleophilic) like carbon-carbon double or triple bond

blocks.prompt: 121 Hydroxide ion reacting with bromoethane to give ethene, water and bromide ion is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Two atoms or groups are removed from adjacent carbons forming a double bond: elimination (19.8).

book_ref.quote: two atoms or groups are removed from two adjacent carbon atoms in molecule

blocks.prompt: 122 In bromoethane, the carbon bonded to bromine carries:
blocks.explanation: Bromine is more electronegative than carbon, so the carbon bonded to Br is δ+ (19.8, book correction).

book_ref.quote: bromine is more electronegative than carbon, so that carbon is +delta

blocks.prompt: 123 Compounds having the same molecular formula but different arrangement of atoms and different properties are called:
blocks.explanation: Such compounds are isomers and the phenomenon is isomerism (19.9).

book_ref.quote: Two or more than two compounds which have same molecular formulae but different arrangement of atoms

blocks.prompt: 124 Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are related as:
blocks.explanation: The same groups are connected at different places: structural or constitutional isomerism (19.9).

book_ref.quote: When same groups or atoms are connected at different places in two or more molecules

blocks.prompt: 125 Isomers in which substituents have different spatial arrangement (different configuration) show:
blocks.explanation: Different spatial arrangement means different configuration: stereoisomerism (19.9).

book_ref.quote: This type of isomerism is called stereoisomerism

blocks.prompt: 126 Stereoisomers are divided into:
blocks.explanation: Stereoisomers are optical isomers and cis-trans isomers (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: Stereoisomers are further divided into two types

blocks.prompt: 127 Optical isomers have identical physical and chemical properties except:

options.text: their ability to rotate plane polarised light

blocks.explanation: Optical isomers differ only in rotating plane polarised light (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: have identical physical and chemical properties except their ability to rotate the plane polarised light

blocks.prompt: 128 A compound which rotates plane polarised light to the right (clockwise) is called:
blocks.explanation: Rotation to the right (clockwise) is dextrorotatory, symbol (+); to the left, levorotatory (–) (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: it is called dextrorotatory indicated by symbol (+)

blocks.prompt: 129 The instrument used to identify and measure optical activity is the:
blocks.explanation: A polarimeter measures optical activity using plane polarised light (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: A polarimeter is used to identify and measure quantitively the optical activity

blocks.prompt: 130 Plane polarised light (PPL) is light which:

options.text: has many wavelengths in all planes
is white light in all directions
has a single wavelength and moves in only one plane

blocks.explanation: PPL is monochromatic light of a single wavelength moving only in one plane (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: PPL is a monochromatic light having single wavelength which moves only in one plane

blocks.prompt: 131 The basic requirement for a compound to be optically active is that it:

options.text: is non-superimposable on its mirror image
is superimposable on its mirror image

blocks.explanation: An optically active compound must be non-superimposable on its mirror image, i.e. chiral (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The basic requirement for a compound to be optically active is that it is non-superimposable on its mirror image

blocks.prompt: 132 The word 'chiral' comes from a Greek word meaning:
blocks.explanation: 'Cheir' means hand; chirality is also called handedness (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: the word 'chiral' is from a Greek word 'Cheir' which means hand

blocks.prompt: 133 Molecules which are superimposable on their mirror images are:
blocks.explanation: Superimposable molecules are achiral and optically inactive (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: Molecules which are superimposable on their mirror images are achiral

blocks.prompt: 134 A carbon atom bearing four different atoms or groups is called a:
blocks.explanation: A carbon bearing four different atoms or groups is a chiral (asymmetric) carbon (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: A carbon atom bearing four different atoms or group of atoms is called chiral carbon

blocks.prompt: 135 Which compound contains a chiral carbon atom?
blocks.explanation: In butan-2-ol, C-2 carries CH₃, H, OH and C₂H₅, four different groups; the others have two identical groups on every carbon (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: A carbon atom bearing four different atoms or group of atoms is called chiral carbon

blocks.prompt: 136 The four different groups attached to the chiral carbon of lactic acid are:
blocks.explanation: Lactic acid's chiral carbon is bonded to CH₃, H, OH and COOH (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: bonded to four different groups, i.e, CH₃, H, OH and COOH

blocks.prompt: 137 Two stereoisomers which are non-superimposable mirror images of each other are called:
blocks.explanation: Non-superimposable mirror image stereoisomers are enantiomers ('enantio' = opposite) (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: non-superimposable mirror image of each other and are called enantiomers

blocks.prompt: 138 The two enantiomers of a compound rotate plane polarised light:

options.text: in the same direction by the same extent
in opposite directions by different extents
in opposite directions by the same extent

blocks.explanation: Enantiomers rotate PPL in opposite directions with the same extent (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: they rotate the plane of polarised light in opposite directions, with the same extent

blocks.prompt: 139 A mixture containing 50% dextrorotatory and 50% levorotatory enantiomers is:
blocks.explanation: An equimolar mixture of enantiomers is optically inactive and is called a racemic mixture, symbol (±) (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: When 50% dextrorotatory and 50% levorotatory enantiomers are present

blocks.prompt: 140 Meso tartaric acid is optically inactive because:

options.text: rotation by one half of the molecule is internally cancelled by the other half

blocks.explanation: Meso forms have similar chiral carbons and a plane of symmetry; the two halves cancel each other's rotation internally (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: rotation of one half of molecule is internally compensated (cancelled) by the other half

blocks.prompt: 141 A meso isomer must contain:

options.text: at least two similar chiral carbons and a plane of symmetry

blocks.explanation: Meso forms contain at least two similar chiral carbon atoms and a plane of symmetry (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: contain at least two similar chiral carbon atoms and also possess a plane of symmetry

blocks.prompt: 142 The maximum number of optical isomers of a compound having three different chiral carbon atoms is:
blocks.explanation: Maximum optical isomers = 2ⁿ = 2³ = 8 (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: is given by the formula 2ⁿ, where 'n' is the number of chiral carbon atoms

blocks.prompt: 143 The number of optical isomers is less than 2ⁿ when:

options.text: the molecule has only one chiral carbon
the molecule has two or more similar chiral carbon atoms
the molecule has a double bond

blocks.explanation: The 2ⁿ number is reduced if there are two or more similar chiral carbon atoms, as in tartaric acid (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: This number is reduced, however, if there are two or more similar chiral carbon atoms

blocks.prompt: 144 A molecule with only one chiral carbon atom is:
blocks.explanation: With one chiral carbon a molecule is always asymmetric and optically active; with more than one it may or may not be (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: However, if there are more than one chiral atoms, a molecule may or not be asymmetric

blocks.prompt: 145 Cis-trans isomerism in open chain compounds arises due to:

options.text: free rotation about a single bond
the presence of a chiral carbon
restricted rotation about a double bond

blocks.explanation: Cis-trans isomers arise from restricted rotation about a double bond in open chain compounds (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: due to restricted rotation about a double bond in open chain compounds are called cis-trans isomers

blocks.prompt: 146 Forms of butane interconverted by free rotation about the C2–C3 single bond are called:
blocks.explanation: They are conformational isomers; they interconvert by free rotation and cannot be separated at room temperature (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: are called conformational isomers because they are interconvertable

blocks.prompt: 147 The energy needed to break the π bond for free rotation about the C=C bond, according to the chapter, is:
blocks.explanation: Breaking the π bond needs 263 kJ/mol, not available at room temperature, so rotation is restricted (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: It requires energy equal to 263 kJ/mol, which is not possible at room temperature

blocks.prompt: 148 The π bond of the C=C double bond in but-2-ene is formed by:
blocks.explanation: The σ bond is from linear overlap of sp² orbitals; the π bond from parallel overlap of p orbitals (19.9.1, book correction: p, not ρ).

book_ref.quote: The π bond is formed by the sideways (parallel) overlap of p orbitals

blocks.prompt: 149 In a cis isomer, the two similar groups are:

options.text: on opposite sides of the double bond
on the same side of the double bond

blocks.explanation: Cis: similar groups on the same side of the double bond; trans: on opposite sides (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The cis isomer is one in which two similar groups are on the same side of the double bond

blocks.prompt: 150 Which compound shows cis-trans isomerism?
blocks.explanation: But-2-ene has two different groups (H and CH₃) on each doubly bonded carbon; the others have two identical groups on one double-bond carbon (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The two different groups must be attached (bonded) to each doubly bonded carbon atom

blocks.prompt: 151 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene does not show cis-trans isomerism because:

options.text: each doubly bonded carbon carries two identical CH₃ groups

blocks.explanation: Cis-trans isomerism is not possible if an unsaturated carbon is bonded to two identical groups (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: cis-trans isomerism will not be possible, if one of the unsaturated carbon atom is bonded to two identical groups

blocks.prompt: 152 Compared with the cis isomer, the corresponding trans isomer is generally:
blocks.explanation: Trans isomers are more stable than cis isomers and differ in reactivity and physical properties (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The trans isomers are more stable than the corresponding cis isomers

blocks.prompt: 153 Cis and trans isomers of a compound differ in:

options.text: melting point, boiling point and dipole moment

blocks.explanation: Cis-trans isomers differ in m.p, b.p, dipole moment, density, heat of vapourisation, etc. (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: different physical properties like melting point, boiling point, dipole moment

blocks.prompt: 154 In but-2-ene, carbon atoms 2 and 3 are:
blocks.explanation: C-2 and C-3 of but-2-ene are sp² hybridized; the π bond locks the molecule in one position (19.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The presence of π bond locks the molecule in one position

blocks.prompt: 155 In the synthesis of pharmaceutical products, chirality is critical because it determines:
blocks.explanation: Chirality is a critical feature to determine the safety and efficacy of drugs (19.10).

book_ref.quote: chirality is a critical feature to determine safety and efficacy

blocks.prompt: 156 The two enantiomers of a chiral drug often behave very differently in the body because drug receptors:

options.text: act as highly specific chiral locks

blocks.explanation: Biological systems are made of chiral building blocks; receptors act as highly specific 'chiral locks' (19.10).

book_ref.quote: the two enantiomers of a chiral drug often exhibit vastly different potentials and profiles

blocks.prompt: 157 Thalidomide was originally distributed as:
blocks.explanation: Thalidomide, a tranquilliser, was originally distributed as a racemic mixture (19.10, Figure 19.7).

book_ref.quote: Thalidomide, a tranquilliser was originally distributed as racemic mixture

blocks.prompt: 158 Research on thalidomide showed that the isomer which damaged the fetus was the:
blocks.explanation: The (+) isomer was an effective, safe tranquilliser; the (–) isomer damaged the fetus (19.10).

book_ref.quote: the (+) isomer was an effective and safe tranquilliser, the (-) isomer was the culprit

blocks.prompt: 159 Giving only the pure (+) isomer of thalidomide would not be safe because:

options.text: it racemises rapidly in the blood stream

blocks.explanation: Racemisation of pure (+) thalidomide occurs rapidly in the blood; within 10 minutes it is over 50% complete (19.10).

book_ref.quote: racemisation of the pure (+) isomer occurs rapidly as soon as it enters the blood stream

blocks.prompt: 160 After its withdrawal, thalidomide was later:
blocks.explanation: Book correction: it was approved in the USA in 1998 (leprosy complication) and 2006 (multiple myeloma) with a pregnancy-prevention programme (19.10).

book_ref.quote: it was approved in the USA in 1998 for a complication of leprosy
